research_question: How can a forecasting operator preserve short-range local structure while retaining compressed long-range memory?
intended_takeaway: A local FIR pathway captures high-fidelity short-range patterns, a global SSM pathway carries compressed long-range context, and a fusion operator combines both representations before forecasting.

content_blocks.label: Historical input
content_blocks.description: Observed historical sequence supplied to both pathways.

content_blocks.label: Local FIR
content_blocks.description: Finite impulse response operator for local, high-fidelity temporal patterns.

content_blocks.label: Global SSM
content_blocks.description: State-space pathway that compresses longer historical context into a recurrent state.

content_blocks.label: Feature fusion
content_blocks.description: Combines local and global representations before the prediction head.

content_blocks.label: Forecast output
content_blocks.description: Point forecast or predictive distribution, depending on the downstream task.

panel_plan.claim: Local and global memory pathways process the same historical input and are fused before forecasting.

references.reason_for_use: Reference for selective state-space mechanism and the separation of algorithmic and systems views.
Reference for presenting a structured state-space operator as a reusable sequence layer.
Reference for making parallel information pathways and their fusion visually explicit.

known_limitations: This is a conceptual architecture specification, not an empirical result.
The exact fusion operator and predictive head are intentionally abstracted.
